chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Washa, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding two men who had stolen from the wealth of Allah. One of them was a slave of the wealth of Allah, and the other was from among the people. He said: 'As for this one who is from the wealth of Allah, there is nothing upon him from the wealth of Allah, for one part has eaten the other part.' And as for the other one, he brought him forward and cut his hand. Then he ordered that he be fed with butter and meat until he was cured from it.

key_terms.عَبْدٌ لِمَالِ اللَّهِ: Slave of God's wealth (a specific category of servant/slave owned by the Imam)
key_terms.قَطَعَ يَدَهُ: He cut his hand (standard punishment for theft)
key_terms.مَالِ اللَّهِ: Wealth of Allah (property belonging to the Imam/State)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for stealing from God's wealth versus stealing from people according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) applies the principle of *takhasus* (specificity) by ruling that a slave, being part of the master's property, is exempt from the standard hand-cutting punishment for theft from that same property, whereas a free person is punished. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the status of 'abd' (slave) as a distinct legal entity yet also as 'property' subject to the owner's rights. The detailed mention of feeding the thief until healed underscores the practical application of *i'tilaf* (compensation for damage) alongside corporal punishment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Washa, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding two men who had stolen from the wealth of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. One of the two was a slave of the wealth of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the other one was from among the (ordinary) people. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for this one who is from the wealth of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, there is nothing upon him from the wealth of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. One part has eaten the other part. And as for the other one, so bring him’. So he<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> cut his hand, then ordered than he should be fed the butter and the meat, until he is cured from it’.
